title: Calibration for Freestyle Libre2 not working any more
body:
Since two years I had been working with Freestyle Libre and was really happy with the performance. I did one calibration at every morning and this did really well work for me. Six weeks ago, I migrated to Freestyle Libre2, using Bluetooth. Unfortunately, I found that the calibration was fixed at a slope of 1.0! This does not correspond to my experience at all. As a measure of first help, I decreased the blood glucose targets to the lowest number allowed by AndroidAPS in order to get at least some better insulin administration. But the situation remains bad, with slopes until 1,6 not properly covered by xDrip+. 

xDrip should therefore offer the normal calibration, NOT FIXED at a slope of 1.0, at least as an option.

This is the calibration data of actual sensor
[FSL2-Kalibrierung - Sensor-2020-06-13.pdf](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/files/4821320/FSL2-Kalibrierung.-.Sensor-2020-06-13.pdf)

Additional data for the calibration show clearly the slope SHOULD NOT BE fixed to 1!


![Screenshot_20200801-084816](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7566125/89339806-0cbbcd80-d69f-11ea-965b-257d6986bddc.png)
![Screenshot_20200802-101706](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7566125/89339813-0f1e2780-d69f-11ea-894f-e31b946e3222.png)

I answer myself: in the question (2), OOP2 SHOULD NOT BE ACTIVATED in Xdrip (uncheck enable external algorithm). Otherwise, it will deliver no BG readings. The raw data is different to the libre 2 raw data, since I'm comparing in parallel with two collectors

my experience with this new OOP2

my update of running in different collectors a Libre2 patched app calibrated at its maximum (+20) and oop2 in another collector. I compared both values with finger pricks (aviva accu-chek), and the result is that OOP2 calibrated is innacurate. It needs to be re-calibrated constantly. For instance, a calibration early in the morning with a slope of 0.57 and intercept of 34.9, resulted in too high values. A new calibration during afternoon resulted in 0.73 and 8.8 for slope and intercept. The main problem it estimated a BG of 168 when it was 133, or a value of 55 when it was 70. I understand that the approach was to reverse the estimation, from libre2 BG readings to Libre1 raw values, and from these you applied the Xdrip algorithm. However, my guess is that it introduces the error twice, one from libre2 BG readings to raw values, and then from raw values to Xdrip BG values. The idea is very much appreciated, but the result is not fine yet. As I said above, I think the problem is the inconsistency of Libre2. Sometimes is within an acceptable range of +/- 5 or 10, and sometimes is well above +30. I found that, in my case, and with this current Libre2 sensor I wear, the calibration of +20 is a good estimation, although I know values are higher when BGs are higher than let's say 140 (tonight, it was 170, but Libre2+20 readings were no higher than 147). right now Libre2+20 readings are closer to finger pricks (BG finger pricks around 70). So my conclusion: Libre2 is close to finger pricks when BG is controlled at let's say 100 mg/dl or lower. But the error increases at values above 130-145 mg/dl, so **the offset range of -40/+20 in calibrations seems to be insufficient**. It is, in my experience, unable to reach high values because of the +20 limitation.

I think that the issue can be closed considering the latest developments made by @tzachi-dar regarding OOP2 and the Xdrip version developed.
Further instructions provided by @tzachi-dar here: [https://gitter.im/LibreOOPAlgorithm/Lobby?utm_source=notification&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=unread-notifications](url) 
Summarized as follows (extracted from there):

Latest version of the oop2 can be found at: [https://drive.google.com/uc?id=14QKSvS5gMWseXvbt_CjYqcD7QdT_2HRW&export=download](url)
latest version of xdrip can be found at: [https://drive.google.com/uc?id=1hLE_mWYeC3S84p9nOZUck37lqJHFahhZ&export=download](url)
Notice this version of Xdrip is still different from that downloadable here. We hope @tzachi-dar update this soon.

What one has to do is: 
1) install oop2 and see that it works (just open it). 
2) install xDrip. (you might have to backup your settings and DB, and uninstall the old version first.) 
3) When asked for the sensor choose libre bluetooth. 
4) Start the sensor. 
5) Scan the libre sensor with xDrip it will ask you if to connect to bluetooth streaming. Press yes. 
6) Scan the sensor again. 
7) after about 15 minutes you will be asked to enter a calibration. 


The sensor seems to wake up only once a minute to advertise. 
It has to be disconnected from a running patched LL app to start advertising. 
Please stop or deinstall that app. Then you should see the sensor in the BT scan. 
The UID is the company name with follwing serial number of the sensor.
Please ensure that any app which was prior connected to the sensor is not working. 
Otherwise it will interfere the xdrip BT connectivity as is permanently try to to connect to the L2 again.

Big thanks to all the developers for this
